title: Crew & ranks
goal: Say who is who on board and find out who to ask about something.

l04-01.text: Diego, come and sit with us. Welcome on board. I'm Tanya, the Chief Officer.
l04-01.es: Diego, vení a sentarte con nosotros. Bienvenido a bordo. Soy Tanya, la Primera Oficial.

l04-02.text: Nice to meet you. So you're in charge of the deck department?
l04-02.es: Mucho gusto. ¿Entonces usted está a cargo del departamento de cubierta?

l04-03.text: That's right. And this is James, the Second Officer.
l04-03.es: Así es. Y él es James, el Segundo Oficial.

l04-04.text: Hi Diego. I do the navigation, so you'll spend a lot of time with me on the bridge.
l04-04.es: Hola Diego. Yo hago la navegación, así que vas a pasar mucho tiempo conmigo en el puente.

l04-05.text: And who's that, at the end of the table?
l04-05.es: ¿Y quién es ese, en la punta de la mesa?

l04-06.text: That's Marek, the Chief Engineer. He runs the engine department.
l04-06.es: Es Marek, el Jefe de Máquinas. Él dirige el departamento de máquinas.

l04-07.text: Hello. If something breaks, you call me.
l04-07.es: Hola. Si algo se rompe, me llamás a mí.

l04-08.text: Does the Captain eat here too?

l04-09.text: Captain Andersen? Yes, but he usually comes later. You meet him this afternoon.
l04-09.es: ¿El Capitán Andersen? Sí, pero normalmente viene más tarde. Lo conocés esta tarde.

l04-10.text: Who should I ask about my work clothes?
l04-10.es: ¿A quién le pregunto por mi ropa de trabajo?

l04-11.text: Ask the bosun, Rolando. He's in charge of the ratings on deck.
l04-11.es: Preguntale al contramaestre, Rolando. Él está a cargo de los marineros en cubierta.

l04-12.text: Soup for the cadet? Chicken soup today!
l04-12.es: ¿Sopa para el cadete? ¡Hoy hay sopa de pollo!

x-master.text: The Master is the Captain of the ship.
x-master.es: El Master es el Capitán del buque.

x-2o.text: The Second Officer does the navigation.

x-ce.text: The Chief Engineer runs the engine department.
x-ce.es: El Jefe de Máquinas dirige el departamento de máquinas.

x-cook.text: The cook works in the galley.
x-cook.es: El cocinero trabaja en la cocina.

x-dept.text: There are three departments: deck, engine and catering.
x-dept.es: Hay tres departamentos: cubierta, máquinas y fonda.

p-incharge.text: Who's in charge of the galley?
p-incharge.es: ¿Quién está a cargo de la cocina?

p-ask.es: ¿A quién le pregunto por mi camarote?

screens.title: Lunch with the officers
screens.body: It's lunchtime. Tanya, the Chief Officer, invites Diego to her table in the officers' mess. He meets the people he will work with. Listen first, one piece at a time.
screens.es: Escuchá primero. El texto está escondido a propósito.

screens.q: When does Diego meet the Captain?
Who should Diego ask about his work clothes?

screens.title: Now the whole lunch
screens.body: Play it again. Open the text and the Spanish if you want them.

screens.title: Tap every number
screens.body: The crew of the LNG Horizon. Officers in blue with gold stripes, ratings in orange.

screens.title: The stress comes first
paras: Most ranks have the stress at the start: CAPtain, MASter, OFficer, BOsun.
One exception: engiNEER. The stress is at the end.

screens.title: Finding the right person
list: Who's in charge of the galley?
¿Quién está a cargo de la cocina?
Who should I ask about my cabin?
¿A quién le pregunto por mi camarote?

screens.title: He works, she runs: the -s
paras: With he, she and one person, the verb takes -s.
In questions and with not, the -s moves to does, and the verb loses it.
steps: James doesn't work in the engine room.
screens.avoid: He work on the bridge. · Does he eats here?

opts: The bosun and the Chief Cook
The Chief Officer and the cook
